hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are in full-blown crisis mode as the Red Devils endure their worst start since 1986. With Carrick at the wheel (again), United have been thumped by Como 4-1, beaten by Atletico and Chelsea, and sit below Coventry and Fulham in the table. The Sporting CP preview series reads like a eulogy — £1.15bn debt, Glazer leveraged buyout trauma, Amorim gone to Milan, and now Roma coming to Old Trafford for a potential coup de grâce. Even Everton's dysfunction looks functional by comparison.

daily.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained catastrophically low throughout the day, anchored at a 2/10 across all three snapshots. The mood progressed from morning despair over a ninth straight winless game to midday cataclysm as the table position (17th) and Lisandro Martinez's red card crystallized the collapse, ending in evening crisis mode with historical comparisons to 1986, Glazer debt fury, and accusations of players downing tools. No improvement or relief emerged — only a deepening litany of structural grievances targeting ownership, recruitment, and accountability.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a cataclysmic 2/10 crisis throughout the week, briefly punctuated only by a fleeting false dawn on October 28th when Kobbie Mainoo's return temporarily lifted spirits to 7/10 before injury setbacks and dressing-room fractures crashed the mood back to rock bottom. The dominant arc is one of deepening structural resignation: a nine-game winless streak, genuine relegation fears, unified fury at the Glazers and INEOS, and a pervasive belief that the squad has downed tools have calcified the fanbase into radioactive gallows humor and total abandonment of hope.
